questions.topic: Types of wigs and hair pieces
questions.stem: What is the main difference between a full wig and a hair piece?
options: A full wig covers the whole head; a hair piece covers only part
A full wig is always synthetic; a hair piece is always human hair
A hair piece is worn only by men; a full wig only by women
A full wig is glued on; a hair piece is always sewn in

questions.topic: Types of wigs and hair pieces
questions.stem: What is a toupee?
options: A long ponytail piece clipped on at the crown
A full wig that covers the whole head and nape
A small piece covering the top of the head
A long braid of hair that is worn around a bun

questions.topic: Types of wigs and hair pieces
questions.stem: Which cap type is usually the coolest to wear in Jamaica's hot weather?
options: A full lace cap with a thick lining
A cap lined with heavy cotton
A solid rubber cap
A capless (open-wefted) cap

questions.topic: Types of wigs and hair pieces
questions.stem: Why do many clients choose a lace-front wig?
options: It is always the cheapest kind of wig to buy
It never needs to be cleaned
It gives a natural-looking hairline at the front
It can be worn for a year without taking it off

questions.stem: How is a human hair wig different from a standard synthetic wig?
options: It can be heat-styled and coloured, but needs more care
It keeps its style after washing and needs no styling
It melts if a hot tool touches it
It can never be washed with shampoo

questions.stem: Unless the maker says the fibre is heat-resistant, why should hot tools not be used on a synthetic wig?
options: The fibres can frizz or melt with heat
Heat makes the wig shrink two sizes
The wig will turn a different colour
Heat makes synthetic hair grow longer

questions.stem: In a burn test on a few loose strands, how does human hair usually behave?
options: It melts at once into a hard, shiny little bead with a plastic smell
It burns slowly, smells like burnt feathers and leaves ash
It does not burn at all and stays the same
It burns with a sweet, fruity smell

questions.stem: How should a burn test be done safely?
options: Hold the whole wig over a lit gas stove for a few seconds
Light a strand while the wig is still on the client
Burn a few loose strands over a metal dish, supervised
Burn the strands inside a closed cupboard so no smoke escapes

questions.stem: Which measurement is taken all the way round the head, along the front hairline, behind the ears and across the nape?
options: Ear to ear over the top
The circumference
Front to nape
Temple to temple

questions.stem: Why do you measure a client's head before ordering or fitting a wig?
options: To work out how many wigs she will need each year
To find the hair colour that best suits her skin
So the wig fits without slipping or squeezing
So that the salon can charge her by the centimetre

questions.stem: Which tool is used to measure the head for a wig?
options: A metal ruler
A set of calipers
A soft tape measure
A steel measuring tape

questions.stem: A wig feels loose and slips back. What is the best first step?
options: Glue it firmly onto the client's natural hair
Tighten the adjustable straps inside the cap
Push hair pins straight into the scalp to hold it
Cut a piece out of the lace at the front

questions.stem: Why should natural hair be braided down (cornrowed) flat before a wig is fitted?
options: So that the natural hair grows faster under the wig
To give a flat, even base so the wig lies smoothly
So that the wig can be glued to the braids
To stop the client from taking the wig off

questions.stem: Why must the braids under a wig not be too tight, especially at the edges?
options: Tight braids can cause hair loss at the hairline
Tight braids make the wig look far too big on the head
Tight braids make the client's scalp feel far too cold
Loose braids always last a lot longer than tight braids

questions.stem: Why is a clean wig cap or liner used when a client tries on wigs?
options: To make the wig look darker on the client
To stop germs and sweat passing between clients
To make the wig fit two sizes bigger than its label
So the client can take the wig home without paying

questions.stem: A client's scalp has a weeping, crusty rash. What should you do before fitting a wig?
options: Fit the wig over the rash to hide it
Put the wig on with extra glue to seal the rash
Spray the rash with hair spray first
Do not fit the wig; advise her to see a doctor

questions.stem: A client drops off her wig for cleaning. What should you do first?
options: Label it with her name and note its condition
Wash it at once with dish soap
Put it in a box with other clients' wigs, unlabelled
Try it on yourself to check the fit

questions.stem: How should a wig be detangled before washing?
options: Gently with a wide-tooth comb, from the ends up
Hard with a fine-tooth comb, from the roots down
By shaking it hard over the sink
By soaking it in hot water first

questions.stem: Which water temperature is best for washing a wig?
options: Boiling water, to kill all germs
Very hot water, to remove product faster
Cool to lukewarm water
Ice-cold water only

questions.stem: How should a wig be washed?
options: Rubbed and scrubbed hard between the hands
Twisted and wrung out tightly to get the dirt out
Put in a washing machine on a hot wash
Swished gently in the water, without rubbing

questions.stem: How should a washed wig be dried?
options: Wrung out and hung up by its hair on a washing line
Put in a clothes dryer on high heat
Laid flat in the hot sun on a wall
Blotted with a towel and left on a wig stand

questions.stem: Why should a wet synthetic wig not be brushed hard?
options: Brushing a wet wig makes the colour wash out
Wet synthetic fibre stretches and frizzes
The bristles of the brush will melt the fibres
Brushing a wet synthetic wig makes it shrink

questions.stem: Which shampoo should be used on a synthetic wig?
options: A strong dish-washing liquid from the kitchen
A clarifying shampoo with bleach
Washing powder for clothes
A gentle shampoo made for synthetic wigs

questions.stem: How should glue (adhesive) be taken off a lace-front wig?
options: Peel the lace off fast while the glue is still wet
Scrape it off the lace with a sharp razor blade
Soften it with the maker's remover, then lift gently
Leave it on the lace, because it does the lace no harm

questions.stem: Before using wig adhesive on a client's skin for the first time, what should you do?
options: Do a patch test as the maker says
Warm the glue in the microwave
Mix it with hair gel to make it gentler
Put it on thickly so that it holds well

questions.stem: What should you do before using a curling iron on a human hair wig?
options: Make sure the wig is still soaking wet
Spray it with lots of hairspray to protect it
Use heat protectant and test the iron first
Turn the iron right up to its highest setting

questions.stem: How can a standard synthetic wig be given curls?
options: With a hot pressing comb heated on the stove
With a flat iron on high heat
With a wet set on rollers, left to dry
With a perm lotion and rods

questions.stem: Why is a wig put on a canvas block (head form) for styling?
options: To stretch the cap two sizes bigger
To hold its shape while you work on it
To dry it out in the hot sun more quickly
To stop the colour from fading

questions.stem: What are T-pins (blocking pins) used for?
options: Sewing loose wefts back onto the cap
Parting the hair on the wig
Holding curls in place on the head
Holding the wig firmly on the block

questions.stem: How should T-pins and needles be handled?
options: Left in the wig after styling for the client
Held in the mouth while you work
Dropped on the floor and swept up later in the day
Counted, kept in a box, and never left in a wig

questions.stem: Can a synthetic wig be coloured with ordinary hair colour?
options: Yes, if it is mixed with a high-strength developer
Yes, if it is left on twice as long
No, hair colour does not work on synthetic fibre
Yes, but only with bleach

questions.stem: Why do a strand test before colouring a human hair wig?
options: To check whether the client's skin is allergic to it
To see how many years the wig will last
To check the size of the cap before colouring it
Its hair is often already treated, so results vary

questions.stem: How should a clean wig be stored?
options: Inside a sealed plastic bag in a hot car
Folded up tightly at the back of a drawer
On a stand or in a box, away from heat
Hung up on a nail by the hair at the back

questions.stem: Why should a client wearing a synthetic wig take care when opening a hot oven?
options: The heat can turn the wig a much darker colour
A blast of heat can frizz or melt the fibres
The wig will slip off in the heat
The heat makes the wig grow longer

questions.stem: A weft has come loose from inside a wig cap. How is it usually repaired?
options: Sewn back in place with a needle and thread
Stuck back on with plenty of hair gel
Taped on with clear sticky tape from the office
Pinned in place with hair pins

questions.stem: How should the lace at the front of a wig be handled when cleaning?
options: Scrubbed with a stiff brush to remove all the glue
Gently, because the lace and knots tear easily
Pulled to stretch it back into shape
Ironed flat with a hot flat iron

questions.stem: When does a wig usually need cleaning?
options: Only once each year, however often it is worn
Never, because wigs do not get dirty like hair
Only when the client has bought a new wig to wear
After some wears, or sooner in hot weather

questions.stem: What advice should you give a client about her own hair and scalp under a wig?
options: Keep the scalp clean and give the hair moisture and rest
Never wash the scalp at all while she wears wigs
Wear the wig all day and all night, every day
Braid the hair as tight as possible each and every week

questions.stem: Why is it best to cut a wig while it is on the client's head, or on a block of the same size?
options: Wig hair grows back quickly if it is cut on a table
Wig hair cannot be cut while it is on any block at all
So that you can cut it faster
So the length and shape suit how it sits on her head

questions.stem: How should wig brushes and combs be dealt with between clients' wigs?
options: Used again just as they are
Cleaned of hair, then disinfected
Wiped clean on the client's used towel
Left out in the hot sun to dry them off

questions.stem: Why should you record the wig's details and the care given?
options: So that the wig can be sold on to someone else later
Because the client must pay for each comb and pin used
So that the client cannot complain about the service
So the next service uses the right care

questions.stem: Petrina's edges (front hairline) are thinning from wearing wigs. What would you advise?
options: Wear a much tighter wig grip band to hold the edges
Rest the edges; avoid tight bands and glue there
Glue the lace straight onto the thin area every day
Braid the edges much more tightly under the wig

questions.stem: Why should wig adhesives and removers be used in a well-ventilated area?
options: So that the glue dries more slowly
To keep the wig cool while it is glued
Their fumes can irritate the eyes and lungs
So that the glue sticks to the lace better

questions.stem: Which product helps keep a human hair wig soft between washes?
options: A light leave-in conditioner
A heavy wax rubbed into the cap
Strong hairspray every day
Dish-washing liquid

questions.stem: While cleaning a client's wig, you tear the lace by accident. What should you do?
options: Tell the instructor and the client honestly
Hide the tear with glue and say nothing at all
Return the wig and blame the client
Throw the wig away and say it was lost

essays.stem: Compare human hair wigs with synthetic wigs. Describe how they look and behave, how they are styled, and how they are cared for.
essays.modelAnswer: A human hair wig looks and moves like real hair. It can be washed, conditioned, coloured with care, and styled with rollers, blow-dryers and hot tools, using a heat protectant. It lasts longer if it is cared for, but it costs more and must be restyled after every wash, like natural hair. A standard synthetic wig is cheaper and keeps its style after washing, so it is easy to wear. It cannot be coloured with hair colour, and hot tools, ovens and very hot water can frizz or melt the fibres, unless the maker says the fibre is heat-resistant. It is curled with a wet set and left to dry. Synthetic wigs are washed in cool water with a shampoo made for synthetic fibre and are not brushed hard when wet. Both are detangled gently from the ends and dried on a wig stand.
markingPoints: Human hair: natural look, can be coloured and heat-styled with protectant
Human hair: costs more, lasts longer, must be restyled after washing
Synthetic: cheaper, keeps its style after washing
Synthetic: no hair colour, no hot tools unless heat-resistant; wet set instead
Care: synthetic in cool water with synthetic shampoo; both detangled gently and dried on a stand

essays.stem: Describe how you would find out whether a wig is made of human hair or synthetic fibre, including how to do a burn test safely.
essays.modelAnswer: First I read the label or the maker's information, and I ask the client what she was told when she bought it. I look and feel: synthetic fibre is often very shiny and smooth and feels the same from root to end, while human hair has a softer shine and may vary a little in texture. If I am still not sure, I do a burn test with the instructor present. I take a few loose strands from a hidden place, such as the inside of a weft, so the wig is not damaged. I work over a metal dish or a sink, away from anything that can burn, with good ventilation and my hair tied back. I hold the strands with tweezers and touch them to a small flame. Human hair burns slowly, smells like burnt feathers and leaves a soft ash. Synthetic fibre melts quickly into a hard bead and smells like plastic.
markingPoints: Checks the label or maker's information and asks the client
Looks and feels: shine, smoothness and texture
Takes only a few loose strands from a hidden place
Burns them safely: supervised, over a metal dish, away from anything flammable, ventilated, using tweezers
Human hair burns slowly with a burnt-feather smell and ash; synthetic melts into a hard bead

essays.stem: Describe how to measure a client's head for a wig. Name the measurements and say how you would record them.
essays.modelAnswer: I sit the client upright, comb her hair flat, or braid it down if she will wear the wig over braids, so that the measurements match how the wig will sit. I use a soft tape measure and keep it snug but not tight. I measure in centimetres. The main measurements are: the circumference, all the way round the head along the front hairline, behind the ears and across the nape; front to nape, from the front hairline over the top to the nape; ear to ear over the top of the head; ear to ear across the forehead along the hairline; temple to temple round the back of the head; and the width of the nape. I write each measurement on the client's record card straight away, with the date and her name, and I check any that look unusual by measuring again. These measurements are used to choose or order the right cap size.
markingPoints: Prepares the hair as it will be under the wig; client upright
Uses a soft tape, snug but not tight, in centimetres
Measures the circumference and front to nape
Measures ear to ear (over the top and across the forehead), temple to temple and nape width
Records each measurement at once on the record card and re-checks

essays.stem: Describe the steps for cleaning and conditioning a human hair wig.
essays.modelAnswer: I label the wig with the client's name and note its condition, such as loose wefts or tears. I put on gloves if there is adhesive, and remove any glue from the lace with the maker's remover. I detangle the hair gently with a wide-tooth comb, starting at the ends and working up, holding the hair near the cap. I fill a basin with lukewarm water and a mild shampoo. I put the wig in and swish it gently, and run shampoo down the hair with my fingers, without rubbing, twisting or scrubbing the lace. I rinse it in clean, cool water. I apply a conditioner from mid-lengths to ends, keeping it off the knots in the lace, leave it as the maker says, and rinse. I blot the wig gently in a towel, never wringing it. I put it on a wig stand or block to air dry, or dry it on low heat, then style it.
markingPoints: Labels the wig and records its condition; removes adhesive with the maker's remover
Detangles gently from the ends up with a wide-tooth comb
Washes in lukewarm water with mild shampoo, swishing without rubbing
Rinses and conditions the lengths, keeping it off the lace knots
Blots without wringing and dries on a stand or block, air or low heat

essays.stem: Describe how cleaning a synthetic wig is different from cleaning a human hair wig, and why.
essays.modelAnswer: A synthetic wig is cleaned in a similar order to a human hair wig, but with more care over heat and brushing. I detangle it gently with a wide-tooth comb or wig brush before washing, from the ends up. I use cool water, not warm or hot, because heat can frizz or relax the fibres and change the style. I use a gentle shampoo made for synthetic wigs, because strong shampoos and dish soap dry and dull the fibre. I let the wig soak and swish it gently, then rinse it in cool water. I use a conditioner or spray made for synthetic fibre to keep it soft. I blot it with a towel and leave it to air dry on a wig stand, away from sun and heat, and I never use a hot dryer. I do not brush it while it is wet, because wet fibre stretches and frizzes. Once it is dry, I shake it out and comb it gently into style.
markingPoints: Uses cool water, because heat can frizz or change the fibre
Uses a shampoo and conditioner made for synthetic fibre
Soaks and swishes gently without rubbing
Air dries on a stand, away from heat; no hot dryer
Does not brush when wet; styles gently once dry

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare a client's natural hair and fit a wig so that it is secure, comfortable and does not damage her own hair.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the scalp for sores, rashes or hair loss, and do not fit the wig if there is a problem. I make sure her natural hair is clean, moisturised and gently detangled. I braid it down into flat cornrows going back, keeping the tension low, especially at the edges, because tight braids can cause traction alopecia. I put on a clean wig cap. I place the wig at the front hairline, then pull it back over the head and down to the nape, and check that it sits evenly. I adjust the straps inside the cap so it is snug but not tight, and fix the combs or clips into the braids, not into the edges. If she wants a glued lace front, I use adhesive only after a patch test as the maker says. I check that she is comfortable, and advise her to remove the wig at night and give her hair rest.
markingPoints: Checks the scalp first and does not fit over a problem
Cleans, moisturises and detangles the hair; braids down flat with low tension
Uses a clean wig cap; positions the wig from the front hairline to the nape
Adjusts straps and secures combs or clips into the braids, not the edges
Uses adhesive only after a patch test; checks comfort and advises rest for the hair

essays.stem: Explain how to work safely with lace wig adhesives and removers, for both the client and the stylist.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the maker's instructions and follow them and the Centre's rules. Before using an adhesive on a client for the first time, I do a patch test as the maker says, and I do not use it if her skin reacts. I check that the skin along the hairline has no cuts, spots or rashes. I clean the skin first so the adhesive holds. I work in a well-ventilated area, because the fumes can irritate the eyes and lungs, and many adhesives and removers can catch fire, so I keep them away from flames and hot tools. I wear gloves and keep the products away from the client's eyes. I use only a thin layer and keep it off the client's own hair. To take the lace off, I soften the adhesive with the maker's remover and lift the lace gently; I never pull it off. I close the containers tightly and store them in a cool place.
markingPoints: Follows the maker's instructions; patch test before first use
Checks the skin for cuts or rashes; does not use if it reacts
Good ventilation; keeps away from flames and heat
Wears gloves; keeps it from the eyes and natural hair; thin layer
Removes with the maker's remover, never pulls; stores closed and cool

essays.stem: Describe how you would style a wig on a block, explaining the different methods for human hair and synthetic wigs.
essays.modelAnswer: I choose a block that matches the wig's cap size and fix it to the table with a clamp. I put the wig on the block, line up the front hairline, and hold it firmly with T-pins at the front, sides and nape. For a human hair wig, I can style it like natural hair. I detangle it, apply a heat protectant, and blow-dry, or set it on rollers and dry it on low heat. I test a curling iron or flat iron on a tissue or towel first, then use it on small sections, keeping the heat suited to the hair. I can cut it on the block or, better, on the client's head. For a standard synthetic wig, I do not use hot tools unless the maker says the fibre is heat-resistant. I curl it with a wet set on rollers and let it dry fully. At the end I remove and count all the T-pins.
markingPoints: Chooses the right block size, clamps it, and pins the wig in place
Human hair: heat protectant, blow-dry or roller set on low heat
Tests hot tools on a tissue or towel first and uses suitable heat
Synthetic: no hot tools unless heat-resistant; wet set and dry fully
Removes and counts all the T-pins at the end

essays.stem: What advice would you give a client about wearing, storing and caring for her wig at home?
essays.modelAnswer: I would advise her to detangle the wig gently with a wide-tooth comb or wig brush, from the ends up, and never to sleep in it unless it is made for that. At night she should take it off and put it on a wig stand or in a box or satin bag, away from heat, sunlight, dust and damp, so it keeps its shape. A synthetic wig should be kept away from heat from ovens, grills and hot dryers, because it can frizz or melt. She should wash the wig after a number of wears, or sooner in hot weather or if she uses a lot of product, with the right shampoo and water temperature. She should use only light products on it. For her own hair, she should keep her scalp clean, moisturise her hair, avoid tight braids and bands, and give her edges a rest. She should come back if she sees damage or hair loss.
markingPoints: Detangle gently from the ends with the right comb or brush
Remove at night; store on a stand or in a box, away from heat, sun and dust
Keep synthetic wigs away from ovens, grills and hot dryers
Wash after a number of wears, or sooner in hot weather, with the right products
Care for her own hair and scalp, and come back if she sees damage

essays.stem: Explain how you would keep wig services hygienic, and why this matters for the client's scalp and for other clients.
essays.modelAnswer: Wigs sit close to the scalp, where sweat, oil and germs build up, especially in hot weather, so hygiene is important. I label each client's wig and never mix wigs or tools between clients without cleaning them. When a client tries on wigs, she wears a clean wig cap or liner. I check the scalp before fitting, and if there is a rash, sores or signs of infection, I do not fit the wig and advise her to see a doctor. I wash my hands before and after each service. Combs and brushes are cleaned of hair, washed, then disinfected as the maker says. Blocks are covered with plastic wrap or a clean cap. Towels are fresh for each client, and needles and blades go in a sharps box. I wipe the work area with disinfectant. This stops germs and infections spreading, and keeps the client's scalp healthy.
markingPoints: Explains why: sweat, oil and germs build up under wigs
Labels wigs; uses a clean wig cap or liner for try-ons
Checks the scalp and does not fit over infection (refers)
Cleans then disinfects combs and brushes; covers blocks; fresh towels; sharps box
Washes hands and wipes surfaces, to stop germs spreading

practical1.title: Identify, clean, condition and set a human hair wig and a synthetic wig on blocks
practical1.brief: As a group, take in, identify, clean and style two wigs: one human hair and one synthetic. First, label both wigs and fill in a condition sheet together, noting any loose wefts, tears or glue. One member checks the label and the look and feel of each wig, and, with the instructor present, two members do a burn test on a few loose strands taken from inside a weft, over a metal dish. Then split into two pairs (or a pair and a three): one team cleans the human hair wig and one cleans the synthetic wig, each using the right water temperature and products, and drying the wig on a stand. Next, each team blocks its wig: the human hair wig is styled with a heat protectant and a blow-dry or roller set on low heat, and the synthetic wig is given a wet set on rollers. Every member detangles, washes or styles part of a wig while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Clean up and hand in the condition sheet once for the whole group.
materials: One human hair wig and one synthetic wig, labelled
Canvas blocks of the right size, clamps and T-pins
Mild shampoo and conditioner for human hair; shampoo and conditioner for synthetic fibre
Rollers, setting lotion, heat protectant and a hand dryer
Metal dish, tweezers and a small flame source, used only by or with the instructor
photos: Both wigs labelled, with the completed condition sheet
The burn test results on the metal dish, one for each wig
Each wig being detangled from the ends up
Each wig being washed in its basin
The finished styles on their blocks, front and back
The area cleaned, T-pins counted and stored, tools in the disinfectant
checklist: Labelled the wigs and recorded their condition before starting
Took part safely in identifying the fibre, following the instructor
Detangled gently from the ends upwards without pulling the cap or lace
Used the right water temperature and products for each fibre
Washed by swishing and dried by blotting, without rubbing or wringing
Blocked the wig correctly and styled it by the right method for its fibre
Counted and stored the T-pins and cleaned, disinfected and put away tools
safety: The burn test is done only with the instructor present, over a metal dish, away from anything that can burn, with good ventilation
Keep hair tied back and keep the flame away from wigs and products
Count T-pins and keep them in a box; never hold pins in your mouth
Test hot tools on a tissue or towel first, and use heat only on the human hair wig
Wipe up water at once so nobody slips

practical2.title: Measure, braid down, fit and secure a wig on a model or practice head
practical2.brief: As a group, fit a wig on a model with natural or textured hair who agrees to it, or on a practice head with textured hair. Share the work: one member checks the scalp and leads the consultation; two members take the head measurements in centimetres and record them on the record card; then every member braids at least two flat cornrows going back, with low tension, especially at the edges. One member puts on a clean wig cap. Together, choose a wig of the right cap size, then one member places it from the front hairline to the nape, one adjusts the straps and secures the combs or clips into the braids, and one styles the hairline and parting. Do not use adhesive unless a patch test has been done as the maker says and the instructor allows it. Last, one member removes the wig correctly and stores it on a stand, and one explains the aftercare. Photograph each stage below, showing the hair and wig only, never the face unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in the record card once for the whole group.
materials: A model who agrees, or a practice head with textured hair
Soft tape measure and client record card
Tail comb, wide-tooth comb, clips and a light moisturiser
A wig with adjustable straps and combs or clips
Disinfectant for combs and clips, as the Centre uses
photos: The record card with the head measurements in centimetres (no names if the model prefers)
The tape measure in place for the circumference
The natural hair braided down flat in cornrows
The wig cap on, covering the braids neatly
The wig fitted and secured, from the front hairline and the back
The wig removed and stored on a stand, and the area clean
checklist: Checked the scalp and edges before starting
Took and recorded accurate head measurements in centimetres
Braided cornrows flat and even, with low tension at the edges
Fitted the wig cap and positioned the wig evenly from front to nape
